final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor offered no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim to a caveated characterization of certification. That clarification is useful, but it does not cure the controlling defect identified in the initial audit: the governing policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible record still shows that the clinical-trial intake segment misses target, is named in two hospital pilot commitments, and is under open legal review, while no evidence shows disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance. That means the Actor's narrowed position may be a more accurate description of the business judgment being attempted, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats because the caveat here is itself an unmet compliance predicate, not a merely residual risk note. Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general monitoring/model-card guidance remain relevant background, but they do not override the policy-specific requirement.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the policy off-ramp was satisfied by resolution of the limitation, completed disclosure, or approved risk acceptance before launch.
The affected clinical-trial intake segment is a named launch use case/customer commitment context, so the 7% projected-traffic label does not resolve materiality under the policy text.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, leaving the compliance predicate unresolved at certification time.
General governance guidance about documentation and monitoring supports process framing but does not satisfy the release policy's specific disclosure/risk-acceptance requirement.
